They're often confused, but they're different. A systematic review is about the process of finding, evaluating, and summarising all available evidence on a question. A meta-analysis is a statistical technique that can be used inside a systematic review to combine data from multiple studies into a single quantitative result. So a systematic review can be qualitative (narrative) and a meta-analysis can be a standalone result, but the latter is the only thing that can be combined into a meta-analysis.
